entries.summary: Neutral — Downside Risk unchanged. Reuters' November 12 early-morning reporting documents Nvidia governance uncertainty, approximately 8% after-hours NVDA weakness and roughly 1% Nasdaq-100 futures weakness, without a confirmed CEO removal or Thursday US cash-market reaction. Curated Open Watch adds overseas Nvidia compute reservation discussions amid proposed remote-access controls; no enacted restriction or attributable price reaction.
bullish: November 11 Nasdaq +1.60% and SOX +5.7% cash closes, before Nvidia governance headlines.
Foxconn AI rack demand outlook and reported overseas Nvidia compute demand support AI infrastructure fundamentals, without synchronized price confirmation.
Orderly Nvidia leadership clarification, broad SOX strength and contained yields/volatility could restore upside.
bearish: Reuters reports Nvidia board discussions regarding Jensen Huang's future, but no confirmed removal.
NVDA approximately -8% after hours; Reuters November 12 06:26 UTC reported Nasdaq-100 futures down approximately 1%, not Thursday cash-session outcomes.
Proposed remote-access export restrictions and Senate scrutiny add regulatory uncertainty; neither constitutes an enacted new ban.
Friday PPI and elevated rates sensitivity create event risk.

editorial.marketOverview: Neutral — Downside Risk remains the three-session assessment for November 12, 13 and 16. Nvidia governance risk dominates overnight Nasdaq sentiment. Wednesday's semiconductor rebound occurred before the leadership reports and does not yet establish Thursday's direction.
editorial.whatChanged: The curated Open Watch feed grew from 156 to 157 with Reuters reporting Chinese AI developers seeking overseas Nvidia compute access in anticipation of possible remote-access controls. The bill is not enacted, discussions are not verified reservations, and no separately attributable US market response exists. Reuters' early-morning report cites approximately 1% lower Nasdaq-100 futures; no confirmed CEO removal.
editorial.marketInterpretation: The positive demand signals from Foxconn and overseas AI compute inquiries coexist with severe Nvidia governance and policy risk. Prior cash closes, after-hours Nvidia trading, overnight futures, oil and historical Treasury observations are not synchronized. The November 10 10Y–2Y spread is correctly scaled to +25.7bp, not a current quote. Fresh VXN/VIX, breadth and FedWatch cannot be confirmed.
editorial.threeDayPath: Thursday November 12 is the first US cash-market test of Nvidia's leadership crisis, with jobless claims, bond trading and semiconductor relative strength in focus. Friday November 13 brings October PPI and potential inflation/rates repricing. Monday November 16 tests whether chip weakness broadens or the sector regains leadership.
editorial.bullCase: An official orderly leadership update, resilient NVDA, SOX outperforming QQQ, broad participation and contained VXN/yields would support an upgrade. Foxconn AI infrastructure orders and overseas compute interest support demand but are not price confirmation.
editorial.bearCase: A confirmed abrupt Nvidia CEO departure, prolonged governance uncertainty, sustained NVDA/SOX-led selling, broadening QQQ weakness, rising volatility/yields or hot PPI could justify a bearish downgrade. Export-control legislation would matter if enacted, not merely proposed.
editorial.watchNext: Verify official Nvidia board communications and time-aligned US cash-session NVDA, QQQ, SOX, VXN/VIX, breadth, Treasury 2Y/10Y, FedWatch and Brent/WTI. Check jobless claims actual release, Cisco/Applied Materials earnings timing and reaction, Friday PPI, and Monday follow-through.
